set.approach: Scorpion Buttress is in Britt Nichols County Park. After driving to the top of Callahan Road, come back down and park on the outside of the last switchback you passed on the way up, in the upper clear-cut, where a spur road is blocked with boulders. Walk the spur road almost to its end and take the obvious trail on the left, which runs downhill to the upper part of the buttress. From the top, either rappel in or take the steep switchbacking trail on the right down to the middle of West Gully. Gym Wall is the open steep slab on the left side as you go down the trail. This is the far-left route on the wall, and its top anchors are easy to reach.

review.notes: Park page and area pages: approach; route page: far left. Descent not stated.

set.approach: Start at Anthony Lake and hike the Hoffer Lakes Trail to the higher of the two lakes. A small side valley runs southwest from it, holding the Upper and Lower Walls. Leaving the trail, work up and around the slabs along the lake's south shore into a meadow; the Lower Wall shows on the valley's right side beyond the meadow, and a faint path reaches its base. Angled Assassin pulls a roof to start and climbs a more featured, lower-angle face than the nearby Sticky Nails.
set.descent_text: The route has no fixed anchor of its own; traverse left to the Sticky Nails anchor. There are no anchors suitable for rappelling, so clean it and scramble down the gully downhill (to the right) of the wall.

review.notes: Area page: approach and descent; route page: roof start, no fixed anchor, traverse to Sticky Nails anchor.

set.approach: Start at Anthony Lake and hike the Hoffer Lakes Trail to the higher of the two lakes. A small side valley runs southwest from it, holding the Upper and Lower Walls. set.descent_text: There are no anchors suitable for rappelling. Clean the last anchor and scramble down the gully downhill (to the right) of the wall.

review.notes: Area page: approach and descent; route page: left/uppermost route.

set.approach: Leave the upper climbers' camp on the trail that drops across Forest Service Road 850, then take the Lookout Ridge Trail until just short of the summit of the Panorama Point knoll. Close to the top a side trail on the left leads out onto Panorama Point, with Rabbit Ears in view to the south. Pick the side trail up again and follow it down the knoll's left, back side to the cliff base. The route is on a sub-buttress of Panorama Point.

review.notes: Area page: approach and the wall-level descent options; route page: sub-buttress of Panorama Point. Lead review dropped the descent: too thin to stand.

set.approach: Scorpion Buttress is in Britt Nichols County Park. After driving to the top of Callahan Road, come back down and park on the outside of the last switchback you passed on the way up, in the upper clear-cut, where a spur road is blocked with boulders. Walk the spur road almost to its end and take the obvious trail on the left, which runs downhill to the upper part of the buttress. From the top, either rappel in or take the steep switchbacking trail on the right down to the middle of West Gully. Prayer Wall faces the Gym Wall across the foot of West Gully. You can also scramble to the top anchors of Prayer Wall from the top of the buttress and rappel in, or go left on the pink-flagged trail that leads to the East Ridge and on to the bottom of the Gym Wall. Atonement sits beside the Madrone Crack and has a conspicuous hueco low on the route.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the chained anchor at the top.

review.notes: Area page: approaches and the chained anchor for rappelling; route page: next to Madrone Crack, bolted anchor with chains.

set.approach: Roosters Tail is a smaller pinnacle just northeast of Rooster Rock. Walk to the viewpoint a little way up the trail from Rooster Rock, drop off its top toward the east, and lose some height to the uphill saddle. The route starts at the saddle and climbs past a single bolt to the summit.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: uphill saddle, one bolt, summit. Descent not stated. Loose rock noted on the route page.
